title: Energy Audit Maintenance Log Form
subtitle: An original energy audit workflow that carries planned or condition-based maintenance through safe release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete energy audit maintenance log form for the building energy-use assessment that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when service personnel need one record for maintenance trigger, asset baseline, work-control references, recurring events, readings, deferred defects, and qualified return-to-service approval. The energy assessment lead owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Energy audit maintenance log identity and ownership
sections.guidance: Define the maintained system, service interval, operating owner, and review period.

sections.title: Energy audit asset baseline and maintenance readiness
sections.guidance: Reconcile the exact asset and known condition before maintenance or testing begins.

blocks.label: Planned maintenance task set
items: Reconcile utility accounts, meters, fuels, and baseline periods
Confirm facility use, occupancy, weather, and production drivers
Inventory envelope, HVAC, lighting, water, and process systems
Observe schedules, setpoints, sequences, and representative loads
Collect non-invasive measurements under an approved measurement plan
Normalize or annotate material baseline anomalies
Screen opportunities with assumptions, dependencies, and uncertainty
Identify comfort, ventilation, reliability, and operational constraints
Assign data gaps and technical questions to qualified reviewers
Prepare findings, evidence index, and implementation handoff

sections.title: Energy audit work control and safe service boundary
sections.guidance: Record the qualified roles and controlling references; do not use this log as the controlling procedure.

blocks.label: Service readiness confirmations
items: Current procedure, manufacturer information, and applicable requirements were reviewed
Asset boundaries, every energy source, and affected systems were identified
Authorized, affected, contractor, and operations roles were coordinated
Isolation, stored-energy control, and verification references are complete
Required tools, instruments, parts, and protective controls are available
Test, temporary energization, and return-to-service steps have explicit authority
Customer, public, traffic, environmental, and critical-service impacts are controlled
Stop conditions and emergency escalation path are understood

blocks.label: Maintenance stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: An energy audit is an evidence record, not permission to open equipment, change controls, or perform hazardous testing. Use non-invasive observations unless an approved task, qualified person, suitable instrument, and site procedure control the work. Stop when conditions or system effects differ from the approved plan and route the issue for professional review. Maintenance stays restricted when isolation, stored energy, system condition, or work scope is unknown. Only the designated authorized person may direct changes to controls and the qualified release owner may approve return to service.

sections.title: Energy audit maintenance events, condition, and readings
sections.guidance: Create a traceable history of work completed, condition found, evidence, and deferred action.

fields.label: Wear pattern, recurring fault, consumable trend, configuration change, and supporting evidence

sections.title: Energy audit exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Exposed electrical parts or a panel requiring intrusive access
Unsafe roof, ladder, mechanical-room, or confined-space access
Moving machinery, hot surface, steam, pressure, or rotating equipment
Suspected hazardous material, severe moisture, or poor air condition
Measurement would disrupt a critical process or life-safety system
Instrument rating, method, or authorization is not confirmed
Site condition differs materially from the approved measurement plan
Any observation requires work outside the assessor's competence or scope
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: An energy audit is an evidence record, not permission to open equipment, change controls, or perform hazardous testing. Use non-invasive observations unless an approved task, qualified person, suitable instrument, and site procedure control the work. Stop when conditions or system effects differ from the approved plan and route the issue for professional review.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each maintenance exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Energy audit decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Building energy-use assessment identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
